title: Scene of Death
summary: Crane found on the floor of Dressing Room 1 by the stage manager.
details: Julian Crane lies between the chaise and the mirror, still in his second-act costume. One blow to the left temple. The door was unlocked when Harriet Pell arrived; she says she found it that way.

title: Medical Examiner's Note
summary: One heavy blow. Dead between 21:40 and 22:10.
details: A single blow to the left temple from a rounded, weighted object, consistent with the missing candlestick. Time of death between 21:40 and 22:10.

title: The Prompt Book
summary: Crane exits at 21:40. Cordelia on stage throughout Act 2. The ASM called cues 21:52–21:56.
details: Act 2 up at 21:05. Crane exits at 21:40 (his character's death). Miss Vane on stage continuously until the curtain at 22:15. In a different hand: 'Cues 41–44 called by ASM, 21:52–21:56 (H.P. away)'.

title: Stage-Door Log
summary: Felix Marsh out of the stage door at 21:50, back at 22:10.
details:
Stage-door keeper's log, Friday 18 May.

21:50  OUT  F. Marsh
22:10  IN   F. Marsh

No other company member used the stage door during Act 2.

title: Payphone Call to a Casting Agent
summary: A 16-minute call from the stage-door payphone to a London casting office.
details: Telephone company record for the stage-door payphone: 21:52 to 22:08, a trunk call to Hale & Partners, casting. The office confirms Felix Marsh was on the line the whole time, reading for a part.

title: Box B Latecomers' Book
summary: Box B's door opened at 21:45 and closed at 22:05.
details: The boxes usher's book, Friday 18 May: 'Box B door open 21:45 — gentleman stepped out. Closed 22:05.' Box B was booked to Voight Management, one seat.

title: Pass-Door Key Card
summary: The pass-door key signed out at 21:44 and back at 22:04, initialled L.V.
details: Front-of-house key board, sign-out card for the pass door to backstage: 'Out 21:44 — L.V. / Back 22:04'. The pass door opens onto the dressing-room corridor two doors from Dressing Room 1.

title: The Brass Candlestick
summary: The missing prop, hidden behind the radiator, with a fresh print in retouched gilt.
details: The props master retouched the candlestick's gilt at 21:30. A clear partial print is pressed into the still-tacky paint on the base; it matches Leonard Voight. Traces of blood and hair on the base.

title: Cigar Band
summary: A Montecristo band in the ashtray of a man who never smoked.
details: A cigar band in Crane's ashtray. Crane was a lifelong non-smoker who banned smoking in his room. Leonard Voight smokes Montecristos.

title: Letter from Sheldon Artists, Hollywood
summary: Crane was leaving Voight Management. The agent had been sent a copy.
details: Sheldon Artists confirm they will represent Julian Crane from Monday 21 May. 'As requested, a copy of this letter has been sent to Mr Leonard Voight, whose management ends on the same date.' Received stamp, Voight Management, 17 May.

title: Wardrobe Sign-In Sheet
summary: Cordelia Vane went into Crane's dressing room in the interval. Raised voices.
details: 20:50 — Miss Vane collects Act 2 gown from Dressing Room 1. Margin note in Mae Donnelly's hand: '(raised voices, 20:52)'.

title: Fly-Rail Repair Note
summary: Harriet fixed a snagged fly line at 21:53, in view of two flymen.
details: Flymen's report: 'Line 14 snagged 21:52. H.P. up the ladder and freed it 21:53–21:55. Back down to the corner.' Signed by both flymen.

title: Key-Man Insurance Schedule
summary: A policy on Crane's life. The beneficiary is Voight Management.
details: Ridgeway Mutual key-man policy on Julian Crane: £250,000, payable to Voight Management. The policy lapses the day Crane's management contract ends.

title: Touring Offer to Felix Marsh
summary: A touring company offering Felix the lead 'should the role become available'.
details: Northern Stage Touring: 'We would be delighted to see you in the role of Edmund, should it become available before the autumn.' Dated 10 May.

title: Cold Tea Tray
summary: Mae's tea tray, left outside Crane's door at 22:00. She left Wardrobe to take it.
details: A tray with a pot of tea gone cold, tagged 'Mr Crane, 22:00' in Mae Donnelly's hand. Wardrobe's own log shows her out from 22:00 to 22:03.
